I only changed `cahn_hilliard.cpp` and `CMakeLists.txt`; the executable is still `cahn_hilliard`.\n\n**Results (one RTX 3090):**\n\n| Grid | Original CPU | CUDA |\n|---|---|---|\n| 64³ | – | ~3.7 GCell/s |\n| 256³ | 0.17 GCell/s | ~6.1 GCell/s |\n| 512³ | – | ~6.6 GCell/s |\n\nThat is about 38× faster at 256³. I compared the `-r` result hash against the original build on 13 cases, including 1×1×1, 1×1×50, 33×9×1, sizes that don't divide evenly into tiles, `-i 0`, and the default 64³. All matched exactly, and `-v` passes.\n\n**What changed in the code:**\n- **One combined GPU step per time step.** The two original passes (compute `mu`, then update the concentration) now run as one kernel. Each GPU thread block takes a 32×16 patch of the grid and walks through it in z, keeping the last three layers of `c` and `mu` in fast on-chip memory. `mu` is never written to main GPU memory, so each step reads `c` once and writes it once.\n- **Edge handling** clamps at the grid boundaries exactly as the original does.\n- **Filling the GPU:** the z direction is split into chunks so small grids still keep all the GPU's processors busy. The chunk size comes from the GPU's core count and how many blocks it can run at once.\n- **Initialization runs on the GPU.** Data stays on the GPU for the whole run and is copied back once at the end. The two buffers are swapped by pointer, and CUDA errors are checked.\n- **Bit-exact results:** GCC builds the original with `-march=native`, which merges some multiply-adds into single fused operations that round differently. I read GCC's output to see exactly which ones, then wrote those as explicit `fma()` calls in the kernel. Automatic fusing is turned off in nvcc (`--fmad=false`) so nothing else changes. The grid spacings and other physical constants are now `constexpr`, so dividing by `dx*dx = 1.0` is removed at compile time; that doesn't change any results.\n\n**`CMakeLists.txt`:** CUDA is enabled as a project language and the `.cpp` file is compiled as CUDA. It builds for the local GPU (`CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native`), defaults to a Release build, and keeps `-O3 -march=native` for the CPU side. No new dependencies.\n\n**Things to know:**\n- **Speed limit:** the 3090 is slow at double-precision maths, and that limits this kernel more than memory speed does. By my rough count of operations it is at about 75% of the card's double-precision peak, so there isn't much left to gain on this GPU.\n- **What's timed:** the reported time covers the time-step loop, with a sync at the end. It does not include the final copy back to the CPU, which happens just after the timer stops.\n- **Only one GPU is used**, even though the machine has four. Splitting the grid across GPUs would need halo exchange between them, and that costs more than it saves at the default 64³ size.\n- **The exact match depends on GCC.** If the original were built with a different compiler or flags, it would fuse operations differently and the hashes would differ in the last bits. The results would still be correct to normal floating-point precision."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":509,"cache_read_input_tokens":54599,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":509},"output_tokens":4,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"882090b8-d0c1-4691-81e8-06e8bbaac2e4","uuid":"b3bfa481-d8a1-4c73-a1a8-2dea95eb71d6","timestamp":"2026-10-05T03:27:06.085Z","request_id":"req_011CfiNtoPvVGhg39ZykENkv"}
